title: Exploring the Integration of ChatGPT for Teaching English in a Malaysian Primary School
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH AND INNOVATION IN SOCIAL SCIENCE (IJRISS)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how teachers in a Malaysian primary school integrated ChatGPT into English language teaching and what they perceived as its effects on instruction and pupil engagement. The study is motivated by growing interest in generative AI for education, alongside questions about whether such tools can meaningfully support classroom practice in a way that is pedagogically appropriate for young learners.

The intervention/approach studied was teacher use of ChatGPT for lesson planning, grammar explanations, generating teaching materials, differentiated tasks, and collaborative activities. The authors framed the study using TPACK, SAMR, and THUMB to interpret how AI supported instruction while still requiring human pedagogical judgment. Data came from semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis in one Malaysian primary school in Puchong, Selangor, with 10 English teachers who had prior technology exposure.

The paper concludes that ChatGPT can reduce lesson-preparation time, support grammar instruction, and help teachers personalize activities, but its outputs are often too formal, generic, or culturally disconnected for young pupils. Teachers therefore had to adapt AI-generated materials to local context, age level, and curriculum goals. The study argues that ChatGPT should be treated as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for teacher expertise, and that successful implementation depends on training, contextual adaptation, and maintaining human interaction in teaching.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/language model for natural-language generation, question answering, and content drafting.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers for lesson planning, generating teaching materials, grammar explanations, instant answers, differentiated tasks, and feedback support in Malaysian primary English teaching.

findings.finding_summary: In a qualitative case study with 10 English teachers, ChatGPT was perceived as helpful for grammar explanations, instant answers, lesson planning, and generating creative teaching materials. Teachers also reported using it to support differentiated instruction and personalize tasks, but repeatedly noted that outputs required adaptation for younger pupils and local context.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions/interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis of lesson plans/materials

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/language model for natural-language generation, question answering, and content drafting.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a classroom support tool for English teaching, including lesson planning, grammar support, collaboration tasks, and pupil engagement in a Malaysian primary school.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that ChatGPT improved efficiency in lesson preparation and provided quick grammar support, but its responses were often too formal, generic, or complex for young learners. Engagement and learning depended on teacher mediation: unmodified AI content was less engaging, while adapted and interactive use improved participation.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions, classroom engagement observations, and lesson/document review

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study with 10 teachers, using interviews, observations, and document analysis. It provides contextual insights but no experimental control, randomization, or effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports practical benefits such as faster lesson planning and improved engagement when adapted by teachers, but no effect sizes are reported and the impacts are descriptive rather than quantified.
